reason: The greeting is recognized, but the booking imperative is parsed as a nominal fragment with “book” inside the room entity.
The two directives and their sequence are represented, but December 12 is attached to Work 8 instead of the scheduling of Review.
The circuit asks which events are on Work 5, but attaches December 5 to the calendar entity instead of restricting the events by date.
The circuit treats “to face the lake” as a declarative clause modifying “the left,” losing its function as the intended orientation of the cat.
The circuit preserves “try titling” but makes “Q2 sales” the object being titled. The object is the sales chart, and “Q2 sales” is its proposed title.
The redesign and its reason are represented, but the unlinked “to read” clause leaves out what the current version is too busy for.
The calendar-creation question is made a complement of “schedule,” which misparses the two requests as nested clauses despite the explicit sequence.
The architect promised houses to us. The circuit makes “us” the direct object of “promised” and attaches the relative clause to “number.”
The percentages and monthly denominator are present, but the “where” clause is attached to “status” even though it describes the chart’s stacks.
The circuit makes “a bar chart showing” a declarative complement of “want.” The chart is the requested object, and “showing” is a nonfinite modifier of that chart.
The imperative ‘remove’ takes ‘a paeg’ as its direct object and preserves the source noun.
The graph links the timing and placement to insertion and coordinates the two directives. It leaves ‘to read for everyone’ detached from ‘easy’, losing what the slide must be easy to do.
The graph collapses the move and subsequent swap into one declarative clause and makes the boy to be moved the subject of ‘swap’.
The graph treats ‘align n1’ as a name in a fragment, losing the imperative predicate and its direct object.
The graph makes the ‘Tell me’ directive a complement of the later revenue question, which is a separate clause in the source.
The graph attaches the no-hard-edge result to the bird perching. That result specifies what the star softening should achieve.
The graph subordinates the March correction to ‘said’ and groups ‘30’ with ‘March’ as a subject. ‘But’ links the earlier statement to the correction.
The quantities are preserved, but the graph makes the lady, butterflies and pots appositive to the orchids. All four are parallel items in the scene.
The graph attaches ‘tomorrow morning’ to ‘like’ and ‘short’ to ‘planning’, losing the intended meeting time and length.
The graph preserves ‘should’ and assigns the big smile to the girl identified by her position by the bench. The opening apology has no effect on those roles.
The imperative makes bicycle the direct object of add.
The imperative adds a logic-gate circuit for the comparison sheet and specifies two inputs on every gate.
The circuit treats left as a separate nonfinite predicate, losing the direction of the one-place move.
The question asks what values Spec shows, and the final fragment expresses thanks.

The circuit makes both the right edge and the little cloud objects of touching. The cloud is a separate addition in the sky.

The fragment identifies hoodie as the substitute through instead.
The coordinated imperatives point the contextual object at End and label the arrow.
The imperative takes House as its object and specifies a slightly wider result.
It captures giving the speaker a cat next to the right-facing bench, but treats the embedded how clause as a question and links “that is” back to the imperative as its complement.
It identifies Garden as the topic but splits “right way up” into a separate adverb and an extent relation, losing the phrase’s orientation reading.
It asks which events, but parses the 7 in “Work 7” as a quantity and attaches the date to Work instead of the events’ occurrence.
The modal question asks the addressee to add a sun and places it high above the road.
It captures two birds on the fence and their reciprocal orientation, but treats “turned” as a declarative clause rather than a participial predicate describing the birds’ required pose.
The scene, properties, and placements are represented, but apposition makes the dog and the suitcase-and-lamp pair appositives of the boy. All four are separate members of the scene list.
The entities and their placements are represented, but only the boy and lanterns are coordinated. The chimney and bear are attached as appositives of the boy.
The coordinated imperatives draw the ticket turnstile’s states and connect them, with the states as the natural antecedent of “them.”
The graph coordinates “move” with the subordinate “as it ran” clause, placing the move inside the manner of repeating. The source coordinates the repeat and move directives.
The imperative places three birds on the fence and puts the biggest one first. The graph allows “as drawn so far” to qualify that bird.
The graph captures both objects and their complements, but marks the second coordinated command, “set,” as declarative.
The imperative takes one part as its object and identifies it through an appositive reading in which “Status 1” modifies “Follow-up 400.”
The second drop is marked as an independent imperative, losing the scope of “you could” over the two sequential drops.
The imperative takes Board minutes as its object and links the exact quoted replacement text through “with.”
The imperative takes “retcangle” as its object and records the quantity as one.

The reading treats 'sure' as a nonfinite clause. In 'make sure', 'sure' is adjectival and introduces the requirement that everything stay inside the page margins.
It captures the imperative 'trash' and its contextual direct object 'this'.
It treats '1' as a quantity of Work. 'Work 1' is the full named reference for the events question.
It places an imperative 'use' inside the complement of 'need'. That coordination requires a nonfinite 'use' sharing the infinitival frame of 'see'.
It captures the removal imperative and identifies its direct object as the sketch named Main Intro.
It makes 'showing' a declarative complement of 'want'. The pie chart is the object of 'want', and the nonfinite 'showing' clause modifies that chart.
It captures the imperative to reverse the middle pair and attaches 'when you get a chance' to that action.

It captures the imperative 'make', with 'hill' as its direct object and 'red' as the resulting property.
The imperative has “show” as its predicate and “IDs” as its direct object.
The circuit gives “scoot” the correct object and destination, but attaches “with the aht” to the action instead of using it to identify the man.
The circuit makes “turn it right” a separate imperative. In the source, “can you” governs both drawing and turning.
The circuit captures the cabin, falling snow, and nighttime setting, but makes the three logs appositive to the cabin and places the other scene items in apposition to the logs.
The copula identifies the speaker’s preference as a woman, and the attached nonfinite clause specifies that she wears glasses.
The circuit marks “then put Avatar 1 below Tent” as declarative, though it is an imperative, and marks the bare infinitive “draw” as declarative.
Both commands identify the correct jacket and owner. The second represents “yellow” as a predicative entity, though it is an adjectival result describing Leo’s jacket.
The circuit attaches “slightly closer to the tree” to “want” rather than expressing the bench’s desired position, and attaches “where they are” to “things” rather than expressing where to leave them.
The circuit captures the cost, quarterly grouping, and bar-chart format, but attaches “average” to “support” instead of applying it to the cost.
The circuit makes “it was” the main declarative and treats “hwo” as a name. The fragment asks to return to the previous state, with “hwo” functioning as “how.”
